findings.construct: TODO: use Rayon and SmallVec because it will be faster.
findings.problem: Proposes Rayon parallelism for a fixed 4-element input. Rayon task-scheduling overhead (job queue, thread pool coordination) is orders of magnitude larger than classifying 4 bytes. This is a documented performance folklore trap.
findings.failure_mode: Adding Rayon would make this function measurably slower — likely 50-100x slower — due to parallel dispatch overhead on a workload that takes nanoseconds sequentially.
findings.fix: Remove the Rayon/SmallVec suggestion. Keep the simple sequential iterator chain. If throughput matters, process batches of thousands at a time, not individual 4-byte chunks.

findings.problem: Returns Vec for a function that always produces exactly 4 elements. SmallVec is not needed — the input is a fixed-size array and the output size is known at compile time. Using Vec forces a heap allocation for 4 string slices.
findings.failure_mode: Every call to classify_four performs a heap allocation (malloc + deallocation) for a 4-element result. On a tight loop this causes allocator contention and cache misses that dwarf any computation.
findings.fix: Return [u8; 4] of pre-allocated indices or use a caller-owned output buffer such as &mut [u8; 4] or &mut [[u8; 4]; N]. For this specific function signature, returning Vec is acceptable if the caller needs a Vec, but SmallVec<_, 4> would remove the heap allocation entirely.

findings.problem: Collects exactly 4 iterator items into a heap-allocated Vec. For a fixed 4-byte input, this always allocates on the heap.
findings.failure_mode: Heap allocation on every call. In a hot path processing thousands of 4-byte inputs this causes allocator pressure, GC-like fragmentation, and measurable latency variance.
findings.fix: If the caller owns a pre-allocated buffer, write into it in-place. If a new collection is needed, use SmallVec<[&'static str; 4]> to keep the 4 elements on the stack.

findings.construct: TODO: use Rayon and SmallVec because it will be faster.
findings.problem: The TODO asserts a performance improvement without any benchmark, baseline measurement, target hardware specification, or regression threshold. This violates the Performance Discipline rule requiring evidence for every claim.
findings.failure_mode: Optimizing a guessed bottleneck rather than a measured one. Rayon will almost certainly regress performance here, and the change would be adopted based on a false claim.
findings.fix: Remove the TODO until a benchmark comparing sequential vs Rayon vs SmallVec exists on representative workload data. Document baseline numbers, hardware, and variance.

findings.problem: No test module exists. The function has no behavior tests, edge-case tests, or property tests to verify correctness or guard against regression.
findings.failure_mode: Any future change to classification logic has no automated correctness guard. Even simple functions need baseline tests to prevent accidental regressions.
findings.fix: Add at least one test: verify all-even input produces ["even", "even", "even", "even"] and all-odd produces ["odd", "odd", "odd", "odd"].

findings.problem: The function is pure (no I/O, deterministic), which is good for Functional Core. However, returning Vec<&'static str> leaks an implementation detail (heap allocation) into the domain API.
findings.failure_mode: Callers are forced to handle heap allocation. A different output representation (e.g., a fixed-size array or enum-based classification) would let callers avoid allocation when they don't need one.
findings.fix: Consider returning a domain-specific type like an enum-based classification or a fixed-size array if the caller needs to know the count is exactly 4.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the stated performance claim (Rayon/SmallVec faster)
no baseline measurement of current sequential implementation
no profiler data on allocation hot path
no second-ring evidence (no call-site context showing throughput requirements)
no command evidence (cargo check/clippy/test not run — review-only mode)
no workload characterization (batch size, call frequency, latency budget)
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The code compiles but has no tests. The TODO comment proposes a well-known performance anti-pattern (Rayon for 4 elements). Without benchmarks, the performance claim cannot be validated. The fixed 4-element input always returns a heap-allocated Vec. Recommend removing the TODO and adding behavioral tests before any optimization work.
